title: Stop a sliding carton and push it onto the packing square
instruction: Stop the sliding carton before it falls off the deck and push it into the green square, without lifting it off the deck.
context: At packing and sortation stations, parcels are pushed or slide off a chute onto low-friction ball-transfer tables and keep coasting; the worker has to catch each one before it runs off the end and steer it to the working spot, by pushing rather than lifting. Done by: packers, parcel sorters and warehouse workers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A grey ball-transfer deck (35 x 78 x 3 cm, friction 0.01) lies flat on the table, its long sides parallel to the line through the arm bases, 7 and 42 cm in front of it; it runs from 62 cm toward the right arm to 16 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases, and its left end is an open 3 cm drop to the table. A green square (16 x 16 cm) is marked on the deck, flush with it, its centre 17 cm in front of the bases and 6 cm toward the left arm from their midpoint. A brown cardboard carton (10 x 10 x 6 cm, 150 g, closed and empty) stands flat on the deck, square to it, its centre 31 cm in front of the bases and 54 cm toward the right arm from their midpoint. When the trial starts, the carton is already sliding toward the left arm at 0.42 m/s, parallel to the deck's long sides (on a real table: launched by a pusher or a short chute at the deck's right end). Untouched, its centre comes level with the green square's right edge after 1.5 s, crosses the square's centre line after 1.8 s and slides off the deck's left end after 2.3 s.
scoring: The carton is watched for the whole trial: if at any moment it leaves the deck (its centre no longer over the deck, or its underside more than 1 cm below the deck top) or is lifted (its underside more than 2 cm above the deck top), the trial scores 0, even if it is put back afterwards. Otherwise: 1.0 if the carton ends standing upright on the deck (its top face's normal within 15 degrees of vertical, underside within 1 cm of the deck top) with its whole footprint inside the green square, still for 1 s. Failing that, where the carton is when the trial ends: 0.5 if it stands upright on the deck with its centre inside the green square (but sticks out of it or is still moving); 0.25 if it stands upright on the deck anywhere else; 0 if it tipped over (top face's normal more than 15 degrees from vertical) or is held off the deck.
reset_notes: Put the carton back at its start on the deck's right end and launch it at 0.42 m/s toward the left as the trial starts. Check the carton isn't crushed.
fidelity: The ball-transfer deck is modelled as a flat plate with friction 0.01 (static and dynamic) that overrides the carton's own, so the carton slows at about 0.1 m/s² as it would coasting on ball transfers, without the balls' small bumps or direction-dependent drag. The carton is a rigid box; a real one dents and is lighter at the corners. The 0.42 m/s launch is set directly on the carton when the trial starts.
